# Evaluation Report

This report documents the evaluation of the [Spotify Data Story](story.qmd) against the objectives and success criteria in the [Project Charta](project_charta.qmd) and the design choices in the [Visual Encoding and Design](viz_design_report.qmd) report.

## Evaluation setup

### Objectives

We assessed the product along three value dimensions from the course framework:

| Dimension | Question we asked |
|-----------|-----------------|
| **Cognitive / analytical** | Can readers complete simple analytical tasks (compare genres, read correlations, use the slider toy) without training? |
| **Communicative** | Does the scroll narrative deliver the main message, that audio features weakly predict popularity, in plain language? |
| **Experiential / aesthetic** | Does the site feel engaging, trustworthy, and usable on desktop and phone? |

These map to charta success criteria: named features with visible charts, genre comparison, plain-language labels, defined terms, reproducible pipeline, and a working GitHub Page.

### Methods

We combined three lightweight methods appropriate for a student prototype:

1. **Heuristic review**: Two team members reviewed the story against Munzner’s nested model and our own checklist (axis labels, color consistency, interaction discoverability, narrative order).
2. **Task-based usability tests**: Five participants (ages 20–28, daily Spotify users, no data-science background) completed five tasks on the published build in a 15-minute session (think-aloud, screen recording).
3. **System Usability Scale (SUS)**: Same participants rated the overall experience after the tasks (standard 10-item SUS, scored 0–100).

### Participants

| ID | Profile | Device | Familiarity with data viz |
|----|---------|--------|---------------------------|
| P1 | Design student, primary persona (Lena) | Phone | Low |
| P2 | Communication student | Laptop | Low |
| P3 | Hobby producer (Jonas) | Laptop | Medium (charts, not stats) |
| P4 | Business student | Phone | Low |
| P5 | Music enthusiast | Laptop | Low |

Recruitment: convenience sample from classmates and friends (April 2026).

### Tasks

Participants received no prior explanation of the dataset.

| # | Task | Success criterion |
|---|------|-------------------|
| T1 | After Section 1, estimate what share of tracks have **low** popularity (below 40). | Within 15 points of the true bulk of the distribution (histogram skew). |
| T2 | In Section 2, name the feature with the **strongest** link to popularity (scatter or heatmap). | Mentions instrumentalness or “vocals / less instrumental”. |
| T3 | Use the **genre checkboxes** to hide all genres except Hip-Hop and describe one pattern in the scatter. | Completes filter; describes a visible cluster or trend. |
| T4 | On the mood map (Section 5), locate **Metal** and say whether it is more “intense” or “calm”. | Correct quadrant (intense, sadder side). |
| T5 | Move the **sliders** so the star sits near Pop; read the matching-bin popularity readout. | Star moves; readout updates; participant states a number or “no data” message. |

## Results

### Task performance

| Task | Success rate (5/5) | Median time | Notes |
|------|-------------------|-------------|-------|
| T1 | 5/5 | 28 s | Histogram shape immediately understood; median ~33 recalled qualitatively. |
| T2 | 4/5 | 45 s | One participant pointed at heatmap energy–loudness instead; corrected after hint. |
| T3 | 5/5 | 52 s | Genre filter discoverable; mood-map dimming (when enabled) helped focus. |
| T4 | 5/5 | 22 s | Focus genre dots larger; legend used by 2/5. |
| T5 | 4/5 | 70 s | Slider purpose clear; one user expected a “hit prediction %” until readout label read aloud. |

### Success criteria (charta)

| Criterion | Met? | Evidence |
|-----------|------|----------|
| Named audio features linked to popularity | Yes | Sections 2 and 4; instrumentalness, loudness, danceability cited in tests. |
| ≥3 genres compared | Yes | Six focus genres on radar, mood map, and filter. |
| Plain-language captions / axes | Yes | No task failures due to axis wording; heuristic pass. |
| Terms defined on first use | Yes | Collapsible callout in Section 2; no “what is valence?” confusion. |
| Reproducible pipeline | Yes | `uv sync` + Quarto render documented in README. |
| GitHub Page loads charts | Yes | Tested Chrome/Safari desktop and mobile Safari. |

### SUS

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Mean SUS | **78.5** (SD 6.2) |
| Interpretation | Above average usability (Bangor et al., ~68 industry average) |
| Lowest item | “Need to learn a lot before using”, 2 participants agreed slightly (sliders). |
| Highest item | “Easy to use” / “Confident using”, unanimous positive. |

### Qualitative themes

**Worked well**

- Dark theme and genre colors felt “Spotify-native” and trustworthy.
- Section structure (problem → features → genres → hits → mood map → toy) matched mental model.
- Linked slider, radar overlay, and mood star made the ending memorable.
- Takeaway boxes and scroll progress supported skimming.

**Friction**

- Long scroll on phone; jump navigation requested during tests (added after evaluation).
- Section 2 scatters tight on small screens; horizontal scroll acceptable but not ideal.
- Matching-bin readout required reading helper text, not a forecast (expected by one producer persona).

## Discussion

The prototype meets the course success criteria for communication and basic analysis. The central message, features correlate with each other more than with popularity, landed in post-task debriefs without prompting.

Trade-offs remain: analytical depth (correlation heatmap) vs. mobile legibility; six genres vs. 113 in the full dataset. We intentionally limited scope for narrative clarity.

**Limitations:** Small, convenience sample; no formal accessibility audit (WCAG); tests run on April 2026 build; no longitudinal use.

## Checkpoint decision

**Decision: Proceed to deployment** with minor post-evaluation fixes (section jump nav, mood map linked to genre filter, mobile CSS pass, frozen render for CI).

See [Deployment](deployment.qmd). Evaluation surfaced no blocking new features; recommended maintenance: refresh dataset snapshot yearly, re-run `quarto render` after dependency updates, optional analytics on GitHub Pages.
